cands.bio: Robert Menendez Jr. is a Democratic attorney who has represented New Jersey's 8th District in the U.S. House since 2023. He worked at Lowenstein Sandler and served as a Port Authority of New York and New Jersey commissioner from 2021 to 2023. He lives in Jersey City.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements and voter-guide recommendations listed by Ballotpedia include New Jersey Citizen Action and the Humane World Action Fund.
In 2022 he was endorsed by Gov. Phil Murphy, Sen. Cory Booker, Rep. Albio Sires, and Mayors Steven Fulop, Ras Baraka and J. Christian Bollwage, among others.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Menendez on data centers, development or growth limits, or land protection. We found nothing on homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, police pay and pensions, school choice or teacher pay, or H-1B. His current campaign site lists immigration as a priority but the page we read gave no specific positions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. The gun and abortion positions above come from his 2022 campaign site, and we did not see an updated statement on them. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through the 118th Congress key votes.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: Attorney at Lowenstein Sandler, Port Authority of NY and NJ commissioner (2021–2023, on its Finance Committee, which oversees the agency's budget), and U.S. Representative since January 2023.
qual.why: He holds a law degree, has practiced law, has overseen a multi-billion-dollar agency budget as a Port Authority commissioner, and has served three House terms. That is prior executive and legislative office plus a legal background.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2022 campaign website said he would fight to re-enact the federal assault weapons ban, expand background checks to private sales, and expand the ability to take guns from abusive dating partners, felons and children.

pro-life.evidence: His 2022 campaign website said he would fight to codify Roe v. Wade, repeal the Hyde Amendment, and make abortion medication easier to obtain by mail.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), which requires DHS to detain certain unauthorized immigrants arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting; it passed the House 263-156 and became law in January 2025.

cands.name: Craig Honts
cands.bio: Socialist Workers Party candidate. Ran for U.S. House in New Jersey's 8th District in 2026 and for Lieutenant Governor of New Jersey in 2025 on a ticket with Joanne Kuniansky. No other background found.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Craig Honts was born or raised, when he came to New Jersey, or his work history, education or any offices he has held. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2025 or 2026, and we found no campaign statements on specific issues such as data centers, property taxes, housing, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We also found no documented controversies, foreign ties or endorsements.
